Peter Panzerfaust.note: WWII Nazi-occupied France reimagining of Peter Pan; resistance fighters, real on-screen combat deaths and casualties. War tone, not horror.

Powers.note: Bendis homicide-detectives-in-a-superhero-world noir; graphic on-page murders of powered people, blood, autopsies. Mature crime, not all-ages cape.

Wasteland.note: Oni far-future post-apocalyptic epic; mutants, raiders, on-screen killings and bloodshed across a ruined Earth.

Warlord of Mars.note: Dynamite Barsoom (John Carter) adaptation; explicit sword combat, beheadings, impalings, blood. Planetary-romance sword-war, graphic.

Punisher War Journal.note: Frank Castle mass-murders criminals on-page with firearms; explicit gun deaths, beatings, blood. Mature vigilante action.

Airboy.note: Eclipse 1980s revival of the WWII aviator pulp; real wartime killing, on-screen combat deaths, mature violence (Dixon/Truman era).

Savage Tales.note: Marvel mature black-and-white war/adventure magazine; explicit combat killings (e.g. The 'Nam-adjacent and WWII jungle warfare), blood, non-code violence.

Scout.note: Tim Truman near-future collapsed-America saga; Apache ex-soldier hunts monsters/men, graphic gun and knife killings. Mature post-apoc action.

Tales of the Witchblade.note: Top Cow Witchblade spin-off; bloody supernatural-weapon kills, on-page assault and graphic violence. Mature dark fantasy.

The Demon.note: Etrigan the rhyming demon (Ennis-era run especially); Hell, torture, decapitations and graphic supernatural slaughter. Dark fantasy/horror action.

The Chronicles of Conan.note: Reprints of Marvel's Conan the Barbarian; explicit sword decapitations, impalings, bloody sorcery-creature kills. Classic violent sword-and-sorcery.

Robert E. Howard's Savage Sword.note: Dark Horse mature black-and-white S&S magazine (Conan, Solomon Kane, etc.); heavy graphic bloodshed, decapitations, gore by design.

Gantz.note: Oku's notoriously gory sci-fi death-game; humans forced to hunt aliens, extreme graphic dismemberment and on-page deaths.

Lazarus.note: Rucka feudal-corporate dystopia; the family enforcer 'Lazarus' kills graphically on-page, sword and gunfights, war and executions. Sci-fi action with explicit violence.

I, Zombie [iZombie].note: Roberson/Allred gravedigger-zombie eats brains, solves murders; on-page brain-eating, monster kills and bloodshed in a supernatural-noir.

Gunsmith Cats.note: Sonoda Chicago bounty-hunter gunfight manga; explicit firearm shootouts, killings, car chases. Crime-action, graphic.

Jonah Hex.note: Palmiotti/Gray Western bounty hunter; brutal on-page shootings, hangings, scalping and gore. Mature violent Western (frontier setting, no AniList Western tag).

All Star Western.note: New-52 Jonah Hex in frontier Gotham; same Palmiotti/Gray brutality — graphic gunfights, killings, gore. Violent Western-noir.

Zorro.note: Wagner's Dynamite Zorro; on-page sword killings, soldiers run through, frontier-California oppression and bloodshed. Swashbuckling action with real deaths.

Lost Marvels.note: Fantagraphics EC-style anthology of war/horror/crime tales; explicit period bloodshed, killings and curses in the classic graphic tradition.

The War That Time Forgot.note: DC soldiers stranded among dinosaurs across eras; on-page combat deaths, soldiers killed by dinosaurs and enemy fire. War-adventure with casualties.

Sledgehammer 44.note: Mignola/Arcudi WWII powered-armor soldier vs Nazis (Hellboy universe); on-page combat deaths, Nazi soldiers killed, explosions and blood.

Xerxes: The Fall of the House of Darius.note: Frank Miller's '300' follow-up; stylized graphic battlefield slaughter, beheadings, impalings and blood. Ultra-violent historical war.

Aliens.note: Dark Horse Aliens; xenomorphs graphically slaughter marines/colonists, chestbursters, acid-blood gore. Sci-fi horror-action with explicit kills.

John Byrne's Next Men.note: Byrne's mature creator-owned super-people-on-the-run; notably graphic for its time — impalement, on-page killings, blood (cover-controversy era).

Sandman Mystery Theatre.note: Wagner/Seagle 1930s pulp-noir vigilante; serial killers, graphic murders and disturbing on-page violence. Mature crime-thriller.

Wetworks.note: WildStorm black-ops team vs vampires/symbiote-armor horrors; heavy gunfire, monster-kills and gore. Military-sci-fi-horror action.

Conan.note: Dark Horse Busiek/Nord Conan; on-page sword decapitations, impalements, bloody sorcery monsters. Graphic sword-and-sorcery.

Gotham Central.note: Brubaker/Rucka GCPD procedural; Joker guns down cops on-page, graphic murders, mob killings. Mature crime-noir in a cape city.

Area 88.note: Kawaguchi mercenary-fighter-pilot war manga; pilots and ground troops die on-page in dogfights and strafing runs. War-tragedy with real casualties.

The Legend of Kamui.note: Shirato's feudal-Japan ninja epic; graphic on-page killings, dismemberment, class-war bloodshed. Gekiga violence.

Incorruptible.note: Waid's 'Irredeemable' companion — a reformed supervillain in a world wrecked by a genocidal hero; on-page graphic deaths, mass-murder aftermath. Mature cape deconstruction.

Green Hornet.note: Dynamite (Kevin Smith) masked vigilante vs organized crime; on-page killings, gunfights, brutal beatdowns. Crime-action.

American Vampire.note: Snyder/Albuquerque vampire saga across American history; savage on-page vampire kills, blood, body-horror transformations. Graphic horror-action.

Vampirella.note: Dynamite Vampirella; graphic vampire/demon slaying, blood, gore. Mature horror-action.

Warlord of Mars: Dejah Thoris.note: Dynamite Barsoom prequel; sword-war, beheadings and bloody planetary combat. Graphic sword-and-planet action.

The Programme.note: WildStorm/Milligan Cold-War superhuman weapons reawaken; massive on-page destruction and graphic deaths. Mature superhero-deconstruction war.

Skaar: Son of Hulk.note: Hulk's son on the savage planet Sakaar; gladiatorial on-page slayings, decapitations and blood. Barbarian sci-fi action, more violent than mainline capes.

Lady Death.note: Avatar dark-fantasy warrior-goddess; relentless graphic dismemberment, gore and demon slaughter. Explicitly violent dark fantasy.

John Constantine: Hellblazer.note: 2020 Spurrier Hellblazer; occult horror with graphic deaths, body horror and gory supernatural violence. Mature urban-fantasy.

Sam and Twitch.note: McFarlane/Bendis homicide-detective spin-off from Spawn; graphic on-page murders, mob hits, gore. Hard crime-noir.

Case Files: Sam & Twitch.note: Continuation of the Sam & Twitch homicide-detective noir; graphic murders and crime-scene gore. Hard crime-thriller.

Conan the Cimmerian.note: Dark Horse Conan ongoing; explicit sword slaughter, beheadings, gory sorcery. Graphic sword-and-sorcery.

The Astounding Wolf-Man.note: Kirkman werewolf-superhero; graphic on-page maulings, family murder, blood. Mature horror-superhero with real deaths (no Werewolf tag — Curses/Shapeshifting/Monster Boy stand in).

Savage Avengers.note: Duggan's Conan-meets-Marvel team (Punisher, Elektra, Wolverine); explicit graphic slaughter, decapitations, blood. Brutal sword-and-superhero action.

Alias.note: Bendis MAX-imprint Jessica Jones PI noir; on-page killings, brutal powered violence and adult/dark content (Purple Man arc). Mature crime-superhero.

Animosity.note: AfterShock — animals suddenly gain sentience and wage war on humanity; extremely graphic on-page killings on both sides. Brutal post-apoc survival.

American Century.note: Vertigo 1950s con-man crime saga; on-page shootings and murders in a hardboiled-noir frame. Mature crime-thriller.

Dark Ark.note: AfterShock dark-fantasy — a sorcerer's ark carrying monsters during the Flood; on-page creature killings and bloodshed. Dark fantasy with explicit violence.

Immortal Hulk.note: Ewing's horror Hulk; grotesque on-page body-horror deaths, regeneration gore, people torn apart. One of Marvel's most graphic recent books.

The Manhattan Projects.note: Hickman's secret-history of mad-scientist Manhattan Project; graphic on-page murders, Oppenheimer cannibalism, blood. Dark sci-fi action-satire.

Sabre.note: Don McGregor's pioneering post-apocalyptic adventure; on-page killings and bloodshed in a collapsed future. Mature action.

Rex Mundi.note: Image/Dark Horse occult alt-history murder-mystery; ritual killings, graphic murders and war. Mature historical-thriller.

Mind MGMT.note: Kindt psychic-spy conspiracy; on-page assassinations, psychic-induced killings and bloodshed. Spy-thriller with explicit violence.

The Maxx.note: Sam Kieth's surreal dark fantasy; on-page violence, sexual-assault trauma and gore woven through a homeless-hero/social-worker psychodrama. Mature.

Dept. H.note: Kindt undersea murder-mystery; a killing in a deep-sea station with on-page death and bloodshed under crushing survival stakes. Crime-thriller.

Razorblades: The Horror Magazine.note: James Tynion horror anthology magazine; explicit gore and graphic deaths by design.

Hellboy: Weird Tales.note: Hellboy occult-detective anthology; monster-fighting with on-page creature kills and bloodshed. Dark-fantasy action.

Drakuun.note: Johji Manabe sword-and-sorcery manga (Dark Horse); on-page sword combat, killings and bloodshed. Mature fantasy action.

Bloodshot.note: Valiant nanite-soldier (Swierczynski run); ultra-violent on-page gunfights, regenerating gore, throats torn out. Graphic sci-fi action.

Highlander.note: Dynamite Highlander; immortals decapitate each other on-page (beheading is the core kill) with blood and 'the Quickening'. Explicit sword violence.

Rat Queens.note: Wiebe's raunchy D&D-style mercenary party; on-page gory monster/goblin kills, dismemberment played mature-comedic. Action + explicit violence, lighter tone.

The Wicked + The Divine.note: Gillen/McKelvie reincarnated-gods drama; abrupt graphic on-page deaths — heads explode, characters murdered. Dark fantasy with explicit violence.

Bitch Planet.note: DeConnick off-world women's-prison dystopia; on-page executions, brutal deaths in a blood-sport, graphic violence. Sci-fi exploitation-homage with real kills.

Nexus.note: Baron/Rude — a being compelled to execute mass-murderers; on-page disintegrations and killings, with a satirical-political edge. Sci-fi action with explicit deaths.
